lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Draw the animated graphics that go over a piece of my video (paper cut-outs, typed words, cards, charts, marker marks) as a see-through overlay with its sound, from a list of what appears when", and give it assets (The folder the look's relative file names (faces, textures, recordings) are read from); out (The folder the overlay, sound, timeline and the render's scratch are written to).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:render-a-motion-graphics-overlay and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Draws one spec, a list of timed events ({type, at, ...}: torn paper strips and cards, typed and kinetic words, count-ups, charts and labels, marker circles and underlines, cut-out photos, footage insets, endcards and many more, one module per event type in do-work/overlay/events/), into overlay.mov (ProRes 4444 with alpha), its sound stem sound.wav (every placed sound, plus the voice when the spec mixes one; sfx-only.wav then holds the sounds alone) and timeline.json (every element, sound and placed box with its time), or, with stills, single frames over the spec's still background.
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: record:setting (records:read).

worked_examples.title: Draw a motion-graphics overlay for a video from a timed list of paper cut-outs, type, cards, charts and marks on its own sample

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
